newsitem.title: CHINA: Interview - MasterCard positioning for China market.
newsitem.headline: Interview - MasterCard positioning for China market.

text.p: MasterCard International on Monday officially opened a representative office in Shanghai to help command a share of China's growing market for payment cards, a senior company executive said.
"It's really a recognition by MasterCard of the importance of this market," said Andre Sekulic, MasterCard International's deputy president for the Asia/Pacific region.
"The timing is right for us," he said in an interview, adding MasterCard opened a Beijing representative office in 1988.
The company currently had around 14 million MasterCards alone on issue in China, representing a 70 percent share of the Chinese market, Sekulic said.
Total transaction volume was $75 billion in 1996 and $18 billion in the first quarter of 1997, the company said.

The bulk of MasterCard's payment cards in China are debit cards -- which require a sum to be first deposited in a bank account from which payments can be drawn -- rather than traditional credit cards.
Debit would form the major component of China's developing payment card market, he said.
"China is fundamentally developing an infrastructure to support debit," Sekulic said. "Although credit will form some of its activities, it won't necessarily be the major activity."
The company aimed to at least triple the current number of MasterCards in the hands of Chinese consumers by 2000, he said.

MasterCard also planned to boost the number of its Maestro cards, through which money is immediately deducted from a deposit account at the point of sale, to 20 million from the current one million by 2000, Sekulic said.
China's central bank had shown an interest in introducing cards which carry computer chips to be used for stored value payment cards, he said.
Mastercard hoped to have cards with the new technology on the market in China as early as 1998 on an experimental basis, Sekulic said.
